message.text:
Explicit Go code removes emoji reactions when a user is deleted. The `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` and `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` functions in all three database drivers handle this deletion.

The database schema contains no foreign key cascade on the reaction table. Reactions are deleted by both content ID and creator ID. Evidence is in `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go`, `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go`, and `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go`. Migration SQL files confirm the absence of foreign key constraints.

h05.
explicit Go code; store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/user_delete.go (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`); LATEST.sql reaction tables have no FK/CASCADE

All three drivers run `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?` and also delete reactions on the user’s memos by `content_id`. Current schemas (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql`) define `reaction` with only a uniqueness constraint—no `REFERENCES` / `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
